title: For a compact connected prequantized Hamiltonian action of a compact connected Lie group, multiplicities near the zero moment-polytope vertex have the exact weakly regular orbifold-sector formula of Theorem 1.2
author: Yiannis Loizides
source_version: Official SIGMA 15 (2019) article 090, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2019.090; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof must compute representation multiplicities even when zero is a singular value and the principal cross-section has a nontrivial generic stabilizer. It combines a detailed support analysis of quasi-polynomial contributions with equivariant index localization and stationary phase in a coisotropic normal form. The author identifies all orbifold sectors and curvature terms, then establishes exactness of the asymptotic formula on an entire lattice cone.

source_check.note: The complete original cone multiplicity Theorem 1.2 and all author Sections 2–3 proof are retained, including the introduction hypotheses and weakly-regular cross-section conventions. The new support analysis, Bott/cross-section reduction, generic-stabilizer elimination, coisotropic normal form, curvature substitution and quasi-polynomial upgrade from asymptotic to exact are included. The established Szenes–Vergne–Paradan decomposition, localization and stationary phase remain cited standard prerequisites. All sector phases, normal denominators and ineffective-orbifold generic-isotropy factors are retained; the shorter point-reduction corollary is not separately counted. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: The complete Section2 proof of cone quasi-polynomiality and all of Section3 stationary-phase calculation were read. Previously established Szenes-Vergne-Paradan decomposition and support inequalities are explicitly cited background, as are Berline-Vergne localization and stationary phase. The author supplies the new support case analysis, cross-section and Bott-class reduction, elimination of generic-stabilizer directions, coisotropic normal form and curvature substitution. The final argument uses quasi-polynomiality to turn the finite asymptotic expansion into an exact formula, including ineffective orbifold generic-isotropy factors. This selects the full cone formula, not a separate short Kawasaki corollary.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.2 with its introduction hypotheses: M compact connected symplectic, G compact connected acting Hamiltonianly with moment map mu_g, G-equivariant Hermitian prequantum line bundle L with compatible curvature -2*pi*i*omega and Kostant condition, and compatible invariant almost complex structure. If zero is outside Delta, m(k,0)=0 for all positive k. Otherwise a full-relative-dimensional closed polytope p within Delta containing zero exists, and for a sufficiently nearby weakly regular value xi the exact displayed sector-integral formula holds for every integral (k,lambda) in C_p. Weak regularity means regularity of the principal cross-section moment map into the affine hull I, not regularity of the full G moment map. All Sigma_g, normal denominators, g_L phases, curvature pairing and the factor 1/d for potentially ineffective orbifold charts are retained from the source.
